_README: A-WP2-FREE-HISTORICAL-GICS-CROSSCHECK-EVAL - records every concrete free
candidate source EVALUATED for independently cross-checking Wikipedia-
revision-captured GICS Sector/Sub-Industry values at historical as-of
dates, per CLAUDE.md ('prevent look-ahead'; 'no substitute for historical
GICS') and ADR-0017 (historical GICS is optional research context, never
authoritative, never a trading gate).
Unlike config/data-sources/sp500-historical-source-registry.json (offline
provenance only, nothing ever fetched to produce that file), exactly ONE
candidate here (spdji-msci-gics-structure-change-press-releases) HAS been
used in a real, bounded, recorded experiment -- performed by
scripts/run_wikipedia_gics_sector_crosscheck_experiment.py, never by
loading this JSON file. This file records the EVALUATION and points at
that experiment's evidence; it does not itself fetch anything and does
not re-derive the experiment's result.
Hard rules enforced by
tests/market_data/test_gics_sector_crosscheck_source_registry.py (all
fail closed):
* classification must be exactly one of NARROW_EVENT_SCOPED_OFFICIAL_PUBLIC
or NOT_SUFFICIENT_FOR_GICS_CROSSCHECK - no other value is recognised.
* every candidate.eligibility flag is FALSE, unconditionally:
- authoritative_official_evidence  (never official, regardless of
source_authority - OFFICIAL_PUBLIC here means 'S&P DJI/MSCI wrote
it', not 'this repository's official GICS evidence')
- eligible_for_promotion_without_validation (validation is mandatory)
- substitute_for_historical_gics   (a single named-event announcement
is not the licensed continuous company-level GICS assignment
series ASOF_GICS_BLOCKER requires, no matter how it is used)
* a NARROW_EVENT_SCOPED_OFFICIAL_PUBLIC candidate must declare
source_authority OFFICIAL_PUBLIC, must carry a non-empty
bounded_real_experiment.evidence_path that RESOLVES to a real file on
disk, and that file's own recorded evidence_checksum must recompute
correctly over its own JSON body (re-derived by the test, never
trusted from a label).
* a NOT_SUFFICIENT_FOR_GICS_CROSSCHECK candidate must declare a
rejection_reason from a fixed enum and carries no experiment reference
- there is nothing here that was used.
This registry never authorizes Paper Auto or Live trading, never claims
integration evidence, and never edits strategy parameters (CLAUDE.md). It
never flips ASOF_GICS_BLOCKER (docs/poi/evidence/dataset-v1/asof-gics-
blocker.json), which stays BLOCKED_EXTERNAL / LICENSE_REQUIRED for the
official, continuous, full-window company-level GICS assignment series -
that gap is DEFERRED_NOT_BLOCKING, not closed by anything recorded here.

NARROW_EVENT_SCOPED_OFFICIAL_PUBLIC.description: A free, dated, official-publisher (S&P DJI/MSCI themselves) announcement naming specific companies reclassified between specific named GICS sectors as of a specific effective date. Genuinely official authorship, but bounded to the named companies and named event only - never a continuous, full-universe, or general-purpose GICS series.

NOT_SUFFICIENT_FOR_GICS_CROSSCHECK.description: A candidate evaluated and found insufficient to serve as a free, dated, independent GICS cross-check source - either it is not GICS at all, carries no temporal/as-of semantics, or no free dated historical archive of it could be identified. Recorded so the gap is explicit, never so the limitation can be bypassed.

candidates.source_name: S&P Dow Jones Indices / MSCI joint press releases announcing GICS structure revisions (distributed free, unauthenticated, via PRNewswire)
candidates.temporal_semantics: Each release states a stated effective date for the structure revision (here: after close of business ET on 2018-09-28 in GICS Direct; 2018-09-24 open for S&P DJI index rebalance) and names specific companies moving FROM a stated OLD GICS Sector TO a stated NEW GICS Sector as of that date. This is a real, dated, before/after claim about NAMED companies only - never a claim about any company it does not name, and never a claim usable for any date other than the one it states.
candidates.access_constraints: Freely reachable over plain HTTPS with no authentication, no paywall, and no bot-protection challenge encountered (verified 2026-09-07). Note: S&P DJI's own primary domain (spglobal.com/spdji) returned HTTP 403 when probed directly and was NOT used; PRNewswire is the free, public distribution channel S&P DJI/MSCI themselves used to publish this exact announcement, and is what was actually fetched.
limitations: Only a HANDFUL of companies are named per release (this one: Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL/GOOG), Facebook Inc. (FB), Netflix Inc. (NFLX), TripAdvisor Inc. (TRIP), Comcast Corp. (CMCSA); Naspers Ltd is also named but is not an S&P 500 / US-ticker constituent and is excluded from the experiment's scope) - it is never a substitute for a continuous, full-universe, per-company-per-date GICS series.
Only covers ONE reclassification EVENT (the 2018 Communication Services structure revision); a different historical classification change would require locating and evaluating a different release.

Prose text, not a machine-readable table - the mapping used in the experiment (scripts/run_wikipedia_gics_sector_crosscheck_experiment.py:GICS_2018_COMMUNICATION_SERVICES_RECLASSIFICATION) is hand-curated FROM the release's own quoted text and is verified at run time to still be an exact substring of the retained raw bytes (see _verify_quoted_claims in that script) - it is not auto-parsed.

Being S&P DJI/MSCI's own announcement makes it authoritative for what it explicitly states, but it is still evaluated here as a bounded research cross-check, not folded into the licensed 'official' capability path (asof_gics stays BLOCKED_EXTERNAL / LICENSE_REQUIRED) - a single event announcement is not the continuous, revision-safe, full-window company-level series that capability requires.

bounded_real_experiment.summary: Two real MediaWiki revisions of 'List of S&P 500 companies' (before: 2018-06-30 request -> revision 848091676; after: 2019-01-15 request -> revision 878489286, both page identity/timestamp-verified against MediaWiki's own metadata) were cross-checked, scoped to the 6 named tickers above, against this press release's stated OLD and NEW GICS Sector values respectively (dataset_v1_wikipedia_pit.cross_check_sectors(..., scope_tickers=...)). Result: the BEFORE-transition scope did NOT corroborate (5/6 agree, ratio 0.8333 < 0.90 threshold - NFLX's Wikipedia-recorded 'Information Technology' disagrees with the release's stated pre-move 'Consumer Discretionary'); the AFTER-transition scope fully corroborated (6/6 agree, ratio 1.0). Both outcomes, including the disagreement, are recorded in evidence_path - neither was hidden or forced to agree.

notes: This is the ONE candidate in this registry that has actually been used in a real experiment; see bounded_real_experiment.evidence_path for the full, self-checksummed result.

Admissible only as BacktestQuality.APPROXIMATE research evidence, bounded to the 6 named tickers and this one 2018 event (dataset_v1_wikipedia_pit.WIKIPEDIA_REVISION_HISTORY_EVALUATION['sector_gics']['bounded_event_scoped_evidence']). It does not admit a general, continuous, full-universe GICS/sector cross-check claim, which stays CAPTURED_UNEVALUATED_NOT_ADMITTED.
Does not close ASOF_GICS_BLOCKER; the official/licensed company-level GICS history gap stays DEFERRED_NOT_BLOCKING.

candidates.source_name: SEC EDGAR company-level Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) codes
candidates.temporal_semantics: SIC assignments carry a filing date and can change over time, so a temporal signal exists in principle.
limitations: SIC is a different taxonomy maintained by a different body (the SEC) with different sector/industry boundaries than GICS (maintained jointly by S&P DJI and MSCI). Mapping SIC to GICS is an approximation, not the published GICS assignment, and is explicitly forbidden as a historical-GICS substitute by this task's owner instructions and docs/poi/evidence/dataset-v1/asof-gics-blocker.json.
Never evaluated further for this reason alone - no amount of temporal/dated coverage would make a different taxonomy an acceptable GICS cross-check source.

candidates.source_name: Any source publishing only CURRENT GICS/sector classifications (current Wikipedia table, current issuer/exchange material, current company descriptions) with no dated revision history
candidates.temporal_semantics: None - a CURRENT-only source carries no effective date and no knowledge date. Using it to cross-check a historical as-of claim would back-project today's classification onto history, exactly the look-ahead failure mode CLAUDE.md and this task's owner instructions forbid.
limitations: Explicitly excluded by this task's owner instructions: 'Do not treat SEC SIC, current GICS, current Wikipedia, or company descriptions as historical GICS substitutes.'

Distinct from the CONTEMPORANEOUS Wikipedia MediaWiki REVISION history this same package already uses as primary evidence (dataset_v1_wikipedia_pit.py) - a revision's own immutable, independently-verified timestamp is what makes that path admissible; the CURRENT page alone (as scraped by sp500_current_universe.py) is not.

candidates.source_name: State Street Select Sector SPDR ETF (e.g. XLK, XLF, XLC) daily published holdings, each fund tracking one GICS sector
candidates.temporal_semantics: The publisher's site exposes only the CURRENT day's holdings for free; no free, dated, historical archive of past daily holdings files was identified during this evaluation (a comprehensive per-date reconstruction via generic web-archive snapshots was not attempted for this bounded task and would need its own coverage/access validation before being treated as evidence).
limitations: Each fund's holdings are licensed-GICS-derived (State Street licenses the GICS-sector index each fund tracks), so even a fully validated historical archive would still be evaluating S&P DJI/MSCI's own classifications at one remove, not an independent second opinion.
Holdings reflect portfolio weights and inclusion/exclusion, not a clean, explicit per-company GICS Sub-Industry label - deriving one would require additional, unvalidated inference.

Recorded here as evaluated-and-not-pursued, not as NOT_FOUND_OR_COMMERCIAL_ONLY in the sibling registry's stricter sense: the current-day page itself is free and accessible, but no sufficient DATED history of it was established.
